The plan emerged from a meeting of the Economic Management Team (EMT) in Abuja on Wednesday, chaired by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele. The ministry said the team agreed to implement as much capital spending as possible in 2026, with outstanding balances rolled into 2027.
The EMT also reviewed progress on the 2027 finance bill, which the ministry said would update Nigeria’s tax laws and add to the ongoing tax reform. It said the aim is to ease doing business, lower borrowing costs and channel more financial-sector liquidity into the real economy.
The ministry said the EMT reported that real GDP grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline and core inflation continued to slow. It put October’s inflation reading at 14.06 per cent and described it as a six-year low.
It stated that external reserves stood at about $55 billion and that the exchange rate was stable and appreciating.
According to the ministry, Moody’s and Fitch have both revised Nigeria’s sovereign credit outlook from stable to positive in 2026. It noted that this followed S&P Global’s upgrade of the country’s rating to ‘B’ from ‘B-‘ in May.
The ministry said the team agreed that discussions on the economy and credit ratings should be grounded in data and evidence. It disclosed that it is working to publish finalised financial and economic information on its website before the end of the year.
The ministry said the EMT identified food security and price stability as a key priority under a 90-day action plan approved by the National Economic Council and endorsed by the Federal Executive Council.
It said the team discussed measures to stabilise prices of staples such as cassava, yams, maize and rice. These, it explained, include strengthening farm-input delivery, reducing post-harvest losses and improving the targeting of agricultural support.
The ministry said the EMT reviewed the national gas plan and the power sector’s 90-day action plan, which it noted targets consistent grid distribution of about 5,500 megawatts in the near term.
It added that work would continue on transmission capacity, metering, and the protection of critical electricity infrastructure from vandalism and theft.
The ministry said the EMT also reviewed the draft National Development Plan 2026–2036, which it said is built around seven pillars: macroeconomic stability, energy, industrialisation, infrastructure, governance, security and human capital development. It said members were asked to carry out further review, with feedback to be incorporated ahead of the plan’s launch.
The ministry said the team received updates on the creative economy and tourism sector, including progress on a creative economy bill before the National Assembly and plans for a Presidential Council on Tourism, approved by the Federal Executive Council. It added that the team also received a presentation on Nigeria’s new national digital addressing system.
According to the ministry, those in attendance were the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola; Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe; Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr. Bosun Tijani; Minister of Regional Development, Abubakar Momoh; Minister of Labour and Employment, Muhammadu Maigari Dingyadi; and Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa.
Others named were the Minister of State, Petroleum Resources (Gas), Dr. Ekperikpe Ekpo; Minister of State for Budget, Dr. Doris Uzoka-Anite; and the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Deputy Governor (Economic Policy), Philip Ikeazor.
The ministry said Special Adviser to the President, Dr. Tope Fasua, the Permanent Secretaries of Finance and Transportation, and the Postmaster General, Engr. Omotola Odeyemi, also attended.
